tagline: Along Alabama's highest range until the pavement simply stops.
intro: West of Heflin, State Route 281 leaves US 78 and climbs onto the crest of the Talladega Mountains, the highest range in Alabama. It runs the backbone through the national forest to Cheaha State Park, tops out at 2,407 feet, and goes on south past the Cheaha Wilderness to Adams Gap. There the pavement ends.

The road began as an unpaved forest route called the Skyway Motorway. Since no one knows how long it will finally be, the state numbers its mileposts as a countdown from 500, and the high numbers have led people to suppose a much longer road was always planned. It was not.

moments.title: Cheaha Mountain
moments.text: A USGS benchmark marks the top of Alabama in front of Bunker Tower, a stone Civilian Conservation Corps building, and the nearest higher peak is 106 miles away in Georgia.

moments.title: Bald Rock
moments.text: A wooden walkway leads out to the overlook on the rock where a P-38 flying from Dallas to Atlanta came down in January 1944.

moments.title: Adams Gap
moments.text: The highway gives out here at the fork of two forest roads, one of them part of the old Skyway Motorway it replaced.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Talladega Scenic Drive
